name: Deep Slate-Violet
lede: Deep Slate-Violet is a muted purple-grey, filed by our library as a slate word rather than a violet one.

sections.title: A slate word
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature plate XLIV gives this swatch as hue 61′′′, tone i, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it under grayish purple, about 5.1 units away [1]. Our library groups the name with the "slate" family rather than with [[violet]] or [[lavender]], since slate is the landscape word the compilers used [1]. In the Munsell notation it reads 4.7P 4.0/2.4, a dark, low-chroma purple [1].

The nearest named color in our data is [[dark-hyssop-violet]], about 4.4 units off, with [[plumbago-slate]] close behind at 4.5 [2]. Both sit in the same dim, bluish-purple neighborhood.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The archive holds this color, as photographed, in 78 of 23,781 paintings, rarer than 54 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 11 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.7 per cent of that century's paintings, 2.7 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow [3]. It is most over-represented in France, 2.3 times expected, 14 of 3,443 paintings [3]. The earliest match is a 1441 painting by Filippo Lippi, 471 years before Ridgway's 1912 record, so it is a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph was fabricated against data/graph/fieldnotes — presence count (71, should be 78), peak-decade stat (1.4%/4.6x, should be 0.7%/2.7x per the century fact), a painter claim ("Henri Matisse, 3 of 50 works") with no painter data for this slug at all (ar.pa and ar.pn are both empty), and a country claim misattributed to "Danish paintings" that was actually the France over-representation fact (14 of 3,443, 2.3x). The earliest-match sentence also named the wrong painting (a 1425 Botticelli predella; the real first-seen record is a 1441 painting by Filippo Lippi). Also fixed the name section: it called plumbago-slate the nearest neighbor at 4.6 units, but dark-hyssop-violet is actually nearest at 4.4 (plumbago-slate is second, at 4.5). Rewrote both passages from the real fieldnotes/graph data; removed the unsupported painter claim rather than inventing a replacement.
